findings.claim: The user-match check reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] without checking that "sender" exists. Re-installing an ACTIVE Integration that has no OrganizationIntegration and no "sender" metadata raises KeyError, which returns HTTP 500 instead of the error page.
findings.evidence: build_integration writes sender only if state.get("sender") (integration.py:376-377). The UI pipeline never binds sender (pipeline.py:93). ensure_integration overwrites metadata on existing rows (pipeline.py:38-42). The repo's own test asserts that pipeline-created integrations have no sender key (test_integration.py:302-308). installation.py:44 guards this exact case with `if "sender" not in integration.metadata`. The existing reinstall test (test_integration.py:360-366) deletes the Integration too, so it never reaches this branch. Proposed red test: create the Integration through the setup flow, or with metadata={}, delete only the OrganizationIntegration, then rerun init and OAuth setup; expect the error page, not KeyError. Not run; reasoned by all three seats.
findings.reason: Three seats agree and two correctness seats rated it Important. Before fixing, make the proposed test red, then apply the smallest fix: use .get("sender", {}).get("login") and treat a missing value as a failure. The metadata clobbering in ensure_integration is out of scope for this finding.

findings.claim: The OAuth state parameter (sent at :402, checked at :412) is pipeline.signature. That value is a constant md5 of view class names, the same for every user and session, so it gives no CSRF protection. An attacker can forge the setup callback and bind their own GitHub login (and installation_id) into a victim's in-progress pipeline.
findings.evidence: pipeline/base.py:132-133 computes the signature as md5 of the view FQNs. Ponytail ran a command that prints 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3, the literal hardcoded across users and orgs in test_integration.py:235,242,338,445,737. The house OAuth2LoginView uses secrets.token_hex(), bind_state and fetch_state for comparison (identity/oauth2.py:245-252,318-325). OAuthLoginView binds installation_id from request.GET on any leg (:397-399), so the user-match check can be satisfied with the attacker's identity. The attack requires the victim to be mid-pipeline. Severity: open-code-review and superpowers rated it Important; ponytail rated its composite finding Critical. Normalised to the correctness seats' Important.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. The constant value is confirmed by ponytail's md5 command. Red test: a callback whose state is the computed constant from a different session must be rejected; it currently passes. Fix: generate a random state, bind_state it, and compare against fetch_state.

findings.claim: The authorize URL is built with an f-string, so client_id, state and redirect_uri are not URL-encoded.
findings.evidence: absolute_uri(...) is interpolated raw at :404-408. It works today only because the setup path contains no &, ? or #. oauth2.py:230-238,250 builds the same URL with urlencode(params). test_integration.py:233-236 asserts the unencoded form, which locks it in.
findings.reason: All four seats agree. Minor, so no red test is required. Fix: build the query string with urlencode and update the test assertion at test_integration.py:233-236.

findings.claim: Exceptions from safe_urlopen (network errors) and from get_user_info's resp.raise_for_status() (revoked token, GitHub 4xx/5xx) are not caught, so they return HTTP 500 instead of the error() page.
findings.evidence: identity/github/provider.py:16 calls raise_for_status(). Only safe_urlread and parse_qsl sit inside the try (:423-434).
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats. Not reported or fixed. ponytail: deferred.

findings.claim: Token-exchange read and parse errors are swallowed by `except Exception: payload = {}` without logging. The existing OAuth2 code logs SSL, connection and decode errors separately.
findings.evidence: integration.py:424-428 compared with the error logging in identity/oauth2.py.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat. This is distinct from the uncaught-exception finding: it concerns a guard that is too broad, not a missing guard. ponytail: deferred.

findings.claim: OAuthLoginView (:389-439, used at :344) hand-rolls an OAuth2 flow that the repo already provides. It could be replaced by NestedPipelineView with IdentityProviderPipeline and the registered GitHubIdentityProvider.
findings.evidence: identity/oauth2.py:210-357 already implements the flow. Slack (slack/integration.py:126) and VSTS (vsts/integration.py:433) use the NestedPipelineView pattern. Comments in the patch say "similar to OAuth2CallbackView...". Ponytail estimates about -50 lines. The replacement is reasoned, not run, and its callback URL (/extensions/default/setup/) is unverified.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat, and an advisory seat, so it never blocks. The security losses ponytail listed are split out as separate findings. ponytail: deferred.

findings.claim: The authenticated-user-equals-installer check is skipped when no Integration row exists yet. On Integration.DoesNotExist the code calls next_step() without comparing identities, and build_integration then resolves any installation_id through the app JWT. Anyone who knows the installation id can therefore claim it before the installation webhook lands.
findings.evidence: The `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` path has no github_authenticated_user comparison. The Integration row is normally created by the webhook (webhook.py:200-209). Severity: open-code-review rated it Minor and superpowers rated it Important; normalised to Important.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats. Not reported or fixed. ponytail: deferred.

findings.claim: test_installation_not_found (:379-396) no longer reaches the installation-not-found path. It sends a non-matching state (ddd023d8...), so the state check at integration.py:412 rejects the request first. The 404 branch of build_integration (integration.py:355-356) is now untested.
findings.evidence: The test sends state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, while every other test sends 9cae5e88.... The responses.replace 404 stub is never called. The assertion changed from "The GitHub installation could not be found." to the generic "Invalid installation request.".
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats. Not reported or fixed. ponytail: deferred.

findings.claim: error() calls _(error_short) on a variable, and the call sites (around :468/:471 and :486/:488) now pass plain string literals. makemessages can no longer extract these strings, so existing translations drop out on the next catalog rebuild, and "Invalid installation request." is never extractable.
findings.evidence: Before the patch these were _("...") literals. The Makefile:61 merge-locale-catalogs target runs makemessages. The strings are present in src/sentry/locale catalogs (ro_RO, zh_CN, uk).
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats. Not reported or fixed. ponytail: deferred.

findings.claim: The same Integration row is queried twice. :478 fetches it and discards the result, then :494 fetches it again with status=ACTIVE.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat. Advisory. ponytail: deferred.

findings.claim: The first lookup has no status filter but the second requires status=ACTIVE. A non-active Integration with no OrganizationIntegration now gets the generic error page, where before the patch it continued to next_step/ensure_integration. This is a behaviour change.
findings.evidence: The two Integration.objects.get calls (:475 and :493-497) use different filters.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat. This is distinct from the duplicate-query finding: it concerns a behaviour change, not a wasted query. ponytail: deferred.

findings.claim: The identity check compares GitHub login strings instead of the stable user id, so a user who renamed their GitHub account after installing is wrongly rejected.
findings.evidence: The webhook stores sender.id (webhook.py:205), and get_user_info returns id.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat. ponytail: deferred.

findings.claim: The setup_path + urlencode({code, state}) block, including the hardcoded state hash, is pasted six times instead of coming from one helper or fixture.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat. Advisory. ponytail: deferred.

coverage: Gate not run (benchmark mode): the review is unanchored and no finding has gate ground truth. No seat ran tests, so every finding is reasoned; the only executed evidence is ponytail's md5 command confirming the constant state. Spec axis did not run: there was no spec, and commit messages were not treated as one. Standards axis was thin: no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or CODING_STANDARDS exist, and the external docs.sentry.io/internal standards linked from CONTRIBUTING.md were not fetched (offline). open-code-review skipped tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py under its default_path rule and read it only as evidence; the other three seats reviewed all 3 files. Not checked by any seat: whether the GitHub App callback URL accepts /extensions/github/setup/ (or /extensions/default/setup/ for the proposed NestedPipelineView replacement); the hardcoded HTTP_X_HUB_SIGNATURE in test_github_user_mismatch; whether the hardcoded state is stable across environments. No rejections: no seat report disproves another seat's finding, and pipeline_advancer.py was cleared by all seats as a behaviour-preserving inline of FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR.
